content.text:
**Finding: Compliant — no redline proposed.**

The Agreement imposes no most-favoured-nation obligation on Corio (our party, as licensee/customer of the BuySite software and MarketSite.net Service), and none in our favour either.

What I checked:
- **Full-text searches** for "most favo(u)red", "favorable/favourable", "no less favorable", "best price", "other customers", "similarly situated", "preferred", "lower", "match", "competit" — no parity language anywhere.
- **Exhibit B Pricing (p0148–p0154)** and **Revenue Sharing Fees (p0155–p0161)**: fixed licence, MarketSite access, maintenance and implementation fees plus a two-way revenue share — no undertaking that Corio will give Commerce One terms at least as good as those given to third parties.
- **Exhibit B Payment Terms (sec-17)** and **Section 4 (Fees)**: payment timing, taxes and audit rights only.
- **Section 2 (Grant of Rights)**: the Distribution License (2.4) and New Products (2.9) create no pricing-parity commitment — future products are licensed on "license fees and other terms and conditions as the parties may agree."
- **Section 1 (Definitions)**: no defined parity/benchmark concept.

Since the playbook preferred position (no MFN burdening the Customer) is already satisfied, no edit is warranted. One caveat flagged in the finding: several commercial figures are redacted as "[*]" in Exhibit B and in Section 2.4, so this rule should be re-run if the unredacted schedule contains a best-terms undertaking by Corio.
